_comment: Compatibility list for /compat/ (tools/gen-site-pages.js). One entry per title, one edition per RE note. Statuses come only from measured evidence in docs/re-notes (ingame = gameplay reached but only a moment of it driven); store, demo and archive links were checked live on `verified`. `archive` (an archive.org item page) is kept only when no store sells the game.
_affiliate_comment: Per store name prefix (GOG, Steam, Humble), a link template with {raw} (the store URL) or {url} (URL-encoded). Empty: plain links. A templated link is marked rel=sponsored and disclosed on the page.

editions.works: After a long load the title and Start menu appear, and holding Enter starts the first-person level with weapon and HUD shown.
editions.issues: Loading takes several minutes, and moving, fighting and sound have not been confirmed yet.

editions.works: The table loads, the plunger launches the ball, both flippers respond, and the score goes up.
The 1997 demo reaches the title screen and a single-player campaign, where units can be selected and moved with the mouse; two-player LAN games can be created and joined.

titles.title: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings

editions.works: The trial reaches Random Map gameplay in the browser, keyboard commands work (select the Town Center, train a villager), and LAN games can be joined.
editions.issues: It runs slowly, under 3 frames per second on the test machine.

editions.works: The original trial installer extracts the game, and the game itself starts as far as its licence agreement screen.
editions.issues: Nothing past the licence screen has been tried; menus and gameplay are not reached yet.

editions.works: The beta demo installs, starts the 'First Conflict' scenario, and a party can be selected and moved across the map.
editions.issues: Sound has not been confirmed working and the browser route and speed have not been checked.

titles.title: Age of Wonders II: The Wizard's Throne

editions.works: The beta demo reaches the world map in the browser and armies can be selected and moved; the map no longer draws over the bottom panel.
editions.issues: It only reaches the menu in the browser's threaded mode, and sound and frame rate have not been checked.

editions.works: In the browser the game reaches Mission 01, where the soldier moves with the arrow keys and aims with the mouse.

demo.label: Official demo (Steam, 'Download Demo' on store page)

editions.works: The Alien demo reaches the menu, loads the colony level, and the Alien turns and walks through the corridors.
The Marine demo loads the Invasion level, aliens attack, and the pulse rifle fires with the mouse.
The original launcher starts the single-player demo, the menus work, and the Marine mission plays in the browser with textured scenery, the HUD and working movement controls; game audio is produced.
editions.issues: Frame rate and audio quality have not been checked yet, and it is not on the public desktop.

editions.works: On a test build the demo started a New Game and Alice could be walked through the first level with the keyboard.
editions.issues: That run used an unreleased test build; it has not been rechecked on the current version or in the browser, and the game is not yet on the site.

editions.works: The demo reaches the main menu, plays the opening dialogue and cutscene, and Boots can then be walked up the street.

titles.title: Anno 1602: Creation of a New World

editions.works: The demo starts a new game and the player's ship can be selected and sailed with the mouse; a black screen in the browser was fixed.

titles.title: Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura

editions.works: In the browser the demo reaches the crash site, the gnome dialogue works, and the character can be walked around with the mouse.
editions.issues: Loading is very slow and the game updates only a few frames per second.

editions.works: The original 1998 demo installs and reaches its main menu.
editions.issues: Choosing Boot Camp stops with a missing-map error, so no mission has been played yet.

editions.works: In the browser the demo shows its settings dialog, the title screen and the start of the intro.
editions.issues: The game crashes during the intro, before the main menu.

demo.label: Official demo (Steam, 'Download Demo' on store page)

editions.works: The demo installs with its own extractor and setup, reaches the menu, and the hero can be run along the first level with the keyboard.
The demo reaches its menu, opens the ship-deck scene, and the view turns with the mouse.
The June 1997 demo plays matches in the browser (move, drop bombs, explosions) and two-player network games over the virtual LAN.

Both playable previews (the interactive demo and the Chapters I and II preview) go through character creation and reach Candlekeep with the created character in the world; the non-interactive demo plays its cinematic.
editions.issues: Two loading waits in each preview need a small built-in workaround, and only the start of play has been tested.

titles.title: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn

editions.works: In the browser you can create a character, watch the opening scene, talk with Imoen and move your character around the first dungeon with the mouse.
editions.issues: Sound quality and frame rate have not been checked, and it is not on the public desktop.

editions.works: The game reaches the shooting range, the crosshair follows the mouse, and firing uses ammo and hits the aimed spot.
editions.issues: Only the command-line runner was tested: a full round, scoring, sound and the browser are unchecked.

editions.works: From the main menu you can launch the first moon mission and drive and steer the tank with the keyboard.
editions.issues: Sound, the cutscene videos, multiplayer and the base-building commands have not been checked yet.

editions.works: The GOG release's bundled ScummVM starts the game, shows the Virgin splash and reaches the opening scene with Foster and the cursor.
editions.issues: Playing with the mouse has not been tested, the GOG installer stalls at its first copy step, and the game is not in the app list.

editions.works: The demo's 16-bit installer opens and shows its main menu.
editions.issues: The Install button does not work (the installer stops or crashes), so the game has never been installed or run; work is parked.

editions.works: In the browser, New Game plays the opening cinematics and reaches Jade's first fight, where attacking and running respond to the keyboard.
editions.issues: It took several minutes to reach the fight, some movement keys are not confirmed, sound and frame rate are unchecked, and it is not in the app list.

editions.works: The demo boots through its menus into the tutorial island, the scripted intro plays out, and after it the god hand, mouse-wheel zoom and mouse-drag camera respond and villagers move in free play.
editions.issues: It is extremely slow (the tutorial intro alone takes over an hour of real time), the in-world intro cannot be skipped, some advanced shader effects are not drawn, and a full browser run has not been requalified since recent fixes.

editions.works: Solo matches against the computer play with keyboard control, and two-player network matches between two browser tabs work with both players able to move.
editions.issues: Finding the other player in the network lobby sometimes fails and needs a retry.

editions.works: The main menu works and the first demo level plays: you can walk, turn and shoot, and enemies fight back.
editions.issues: Sound, the original launcher and the browser have not been checked.

editions.works: The demo installs, plays its intro movies and mission briefing, and the battle runs with units selectable by mouse (software renderer).
editions.issues: Battle speed in the browser has not been checked, and it is not on the public desktop.

editions.works: The sliding-block puzzle starts, blocks can be dragged with the mouse, moves are counted and the sound toggle shortcut works, in the browser too.

titles.title: Broken Sword: The Shadow of the Templars

editions.works: The original installer completes, the opening movie plays, and in the café scene the cursor changes over hotspots and clicking walks George around the square.
From the title screen you can start a new game, type your governor's name, read the first assignment and reach the live city.
editions.issues: The automated check stops once the city is live; building and later play are not separately recorded.

editions.works: The original installer runs, and from the main menu you can start Demo Level 1 (La Roca) and move Claw through the level with the arrow keys.
The demo installs, plays its intro, and the race starts; the car responds to accelerate, brake and steer keys until the demo's timer ends it.
editions.issues: The original launcher program does not work (the game is started directly), and the browser is unchecked.

editions.works: The alpha test demo launches through its launcher into a race in the browser, where accelerating, reversing and braking work.
editions.issues: Steering has not been confirmed separately, a full race, sound and frame rate are unchecked, and the loading screen is long.

editions.works: Chip moves through the level with the arrow keys, and the background music option plays.

editions.issues: It stops during startup, before any window is drawn.

editions.works: Goes from the options screen through the service area into the Corrigin stage, where the stage clock runs and the car accelerates and steers from the keyboard.
editions.issues: Sound and the browser version have not been checked.

editions.works: From the menus you can start a rally stage and drive the car, with correct textures, car lighting and menu text.
editions.issues: The menu soon drops into the attract demo if left idle, the game's own installer does not run, and night stages and the browser are unchecked.

editions.works: The title screen and menus work, and you can choose a car and a stage.
editions.issues: Loading the stage fails with a graphics error, so no race has been driven.

editions.works: In the browser the game plays through 180 clicks to level 2 with no crash.
editions.issues: The frame rate is low and uneven, and the game needs an 800x600 screen.

editions.works: The DOS demo reaches the cockpit through its normal menus and the helicopter flies forward and banks under keyboard control.
editions.issues: Getting to the cockpit took about 45 minutes of loading, and sound is turned off; combat and missions were not tested.

editions.works: Goes through the pilot and mission menus to the briefing, launches the mission, and the helicopter lifts off and climbs under keyboard control, both headless and in the browser page.
editions.issues: Mission loading takes a long time; combat and finishing a mission were not tested.

editions.works: The first Allied mission starts from the main menu, and units can be selected and ordered to move.
editions.issues: Mouse clicks land offset from where they appear on screen, and sound and the browser have not been checked.

editions.works: The main menu draws with all its buttons, and New Campaign opens its dialog.
editions.issues: Loading the campaign crashes before the mission starts.

editions.works: Reaches the main menu and the first mission briefing with voice-over; in the mission a commando can be selected and walked across the map with the mouse, and the music plays at the data level.
editions.issues: The browser version, real audio output and frame rate have not been checked.

editions.works: The demo installer ran through its language, welcome and destination screens to the license agreement.
editions.issues: Installation was never completed and the installer files are currently unavailable, so the game itself has not been run.

editions.works: The DOS demo starts and runs its initialization.
editions.issues: It stops with a 'No Graphics hardware detected' error before showing any graphics, so no menu or gameplay is reached.

editions.works: Shows the attract mode and the Jungle/Mine/Options menu, and in the Jungle level Croc turns and moves along the path from the keyboard in the browser.
editions.issues: The ground sometimes shows black holes where triangles are missing; sound and longer play were not checked.

editions.works: A deal fills the maximized window, cards can be moved, and Deal regathers the piles.
editions.issues: The Game menu's shortcut labels show garbled characters.

editions.works: With the software renderer the title and menus draw correctly, New Game loads the first level, and the hero turns and walks from the keyboard.
editions.issues: Only the software renderer and the start of the level were tested; sound was not checked.

editions.works: The installed demo boots to the main menu, picking a difficulty loads the first swamp level, and the player can walk forward and pick up a weapon, in the browser as well.
The magazine demo goes from the intro through the campaign menus into the first Mars mission, where a unit can be built with Space and the map scrolled with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: Clicking the sidebar Build button did nothing (Space works instead) and typing a leader name showed no text; sound and speed are untested.

editions.works: Installed from the demo CD, it goes through the settings screens and main menu into a new game, where Arkhan can be walked out of his room into the domed hall.
editions.issues: Sound, speed and the browser route have not been checked.

editions.works: After networking fixes the demo starts, passes its graphics and network checks and loads its menu shell for 30 seconds without crashing.
editions.issues: The menu has not been shown working with input and no mission has been played.

titles.title: Dark Reign: The Future of War

editions.works: The demo reaches the main menu and loads the Training 2 mission, where the briefing can be closed and units selected and ordered with the mouse.
editions.issues: Multiplayer is untried.

editions.works: Character creation leads into Town, where the camera can be turned and the hero walked by clicking; two-player games over the virtual LAN also reach Town together.
editions.issues: The WebGL and software renderers draw some scenes differently, with a black wedge in the lower-left of the view, and combat, sound and speed are untested.

editions.works: The demo goes from the attract mode through the title menu and car settings into an Arcade race, where holding gas drives the car to 163 mph.
editions.issues: Steering, sound, speed and the network modes have not been checked.

editions.works: With the software renderer, the demo goes through soldier selection and the main menu into mission 1, where the player can look around, walk past the first checkpoint and get shot by enemies.
editions.issues: Speed in the browser has not been measured.

editions.works: With OpenGL, the demo goes through pilot creation and the main menu into the first level, where the ship can turn and fire its laser.
editions.issues: Loading the level takes a very long time.

editions.works: You can make a pilot, walk from the main hall into the ready room, launch the first training mission and fly it with voice playing, and targeting works.
editions.issues: Frame rate and the browser version have not been checked yet.

editions.works: With Direct3D picked in the startup dialog, the demo reaches the menus and a full race where the car accelerates and overtakes, on desktop and on an iPhone.
editions.issues: The default 3Dfx Glide option in the startup dialog crashes, so Direct3D has to be chosen by hand, and firing has not been confirmed.

editions.works: The demo goes from the intro and main menu into the Training map, where JC can be walked through the level with the keyboard, with the software and Direct3D renderers.
editions.issues: It runs at only about 5 to 10 frames per second, Direct3D is darker than it should be, and the Glide and OpenGL renderers do not work in the browser.

editions.works: The demo opens its game window and the launcher hands off to the level process, but it stays on the loading screen.
editions.issues: It never gets past the loading screen to the menu or gameplay.

editions.works: The August 1996 demo goes from New Game through class and name selection into Tristram, where the warrior walks on click and the inventory opens.
editions.issues: In the browser, Backspace cannot edit the hero name.

editions.works: The retail CD installs and passes its disc check, then goes through the menus and hero creation into Tristram with a controllable warrior, both from the command line and in the browser.
The shareware version goes from the menus through hero creation into Tristram, where the warrior walks on click and the character and inventory panels open, at the game's normal 20 frames per second.
editions.issues: In the browser the final full-screen picture sometimes loses artwork.

demo.label: Diablo Shareware CD (Blizzard shareware, freely redistributable)

editions.works: The demo installs, creates a Barbarian and reaches the Rogue Encampment, where clicking the ground moves the hero, in the browser with both the WebGL and software renderers; the Glide version's menu music plays continuously.
editions.issues: Sound in town, combat and longer sessions have not been checked.

editions.works: With software rendering, and with the default 3Dfx option after a fix, the demo reaches the main menu and the first Quest level, where Enric can be walked to the barred gate.
editions.issues: The menu mouse misses its targets, so menus are driven with the keyboard; sound and speed are untested.

editions.works: Starting a new game on Easy goes through loading and the intro into the first level, where you can walk and look around with the full HUD.
editions.issues: Only tested from the command line so far, and slowly; the browser version, frame rate and sound have not been checked.

editions.works: In the browser you can start a quest, select your leader and move him across the map at about 27 frames per second, with music and sound playing.
The intro and main menu work, and a new saga can be started through race and lord choice to the adventure map and city screen.
editions.issues: In the browser only the main menu has been checked; sound, frame rate, battles and multiplayer have not been tested.

editions.works: New Game reaches the first level, riding the dragon in the rain with enemies and the HUD, both from the command line and in the browser.
editions.issues: In one browser run the game dropped back to the menu for an unknown reason, and frame rate and sound have not been checked.

editions.works: The attract mode, front end and the 'Lose the tail!' chase work, and the car can be driven out of the garage using the 3dfx Glide renderer.
editions.issues: Needs the game's Config to be run once first and only the Glide option is offered; the browser version and frame rate have not been checked.

editions.works: The logos and main menu work, the cursor can be moved, and Start New Game enters the first dungeon with its tutorial panel.
editions.issues: Actually playing the level has not been tested, and quick single mouse jumps can occasionally be missed.

editions.works: Character creation works and the outdoor world loads, where the character can be moved with the keyboard.
editions.issues: The 3D world runs extremely slowly (well under one frame per second when measured) and needs a larger memory setting.

editions.works: The game starts and shows its licence agreement, and accepting it opens the game window.
editions.issues: Right after the licence it stops with a 'resource read error' on its data file, so no menu or gameplay yet.

editions.works: The game starts and shows a readable licence agreement.
editions.issues: Nothing past the licence screen has been tried yet.

editions.works: In the browser the launcher, main menu and character setup work, and the hero can be walked around the first dungeon level with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: Only a short stretch of play has been tested; sound quality and frame rate have not been checked.

editions.works: The game plays in the browser with touch steering, in both portrait and landscape layouts.
editions.issues: A memory fix for a crash seen on iPhone has not yet been re-tested on a real device.

editions.works: The menus and levels work: the bike can be ridden through a level with the keyboard, and game sound plays in the browser.
The title screen comes up with music, and clicking Next starts a pipe board showing the START and FINISH pipes.
editions.issues: Actually laying pipe and finishing a level has not been tested yet.

editions.works: The main menu, team selection and mission briefing all work, and the first jungle mission loads with the squad views and radar showing.
editions.issues: Moving and shooting in the mission has not been tested, the level takes a long time to load, and sound and the video clips have not been checked.

editions.works: From the launcher and main menu you can start the first mission, spawn your soldier and walk him down the street until an enemy shows up.
editions.issues: After a few minutes of play the game drops back to the main menu, probably because the level timer runs out, and nobody has looked into it yet.

editions.works: You can start a new game as Max Stone, walk around the first map, open the inventory and equip items, aim and fire a weapon in combat, and this was also tested in the browser.
editions.issues: Some spots on the map you click could not be walked to (not yet known whether that is the game or the emulator), and conversations, full combat rounds and sound have not been checked.

editions.works: In the browser you can go through the menus, set up the keyboard as a controller and start a friendly England v Italy match, and the selected player moves when you press the arrow keys.
editions.issues: Controls have only been partly checked, there is no touch layout, and sound and frame rate have not been checked.

editions.works: GOG's ScummVM build starts the game and shows the title screen, and a longer scripted run got as far as Joe standing in the first room with the verb and inventory bar.
editions.issues: The GOG installer does not finish inside the emulator (the files had to be unpacked separately), and actually playing through puzzles has not been tested.

editions.works: The intro, cutscenes and the first room play; hovering shows action hints and clicking walks Joe around the room.
editions.issues: The newer GOG ScummVM build does not start.

editions.works: You can start a single-player game and fly into the Volcano level with the full HUD, and firing the main weapon works.
editions.issues: The intro and menu screens look heavily washed out to white, and most of the movement controls have not been tested.

editions.works: You can start a game and drop a stone, and the computer answers with its own move.
A game deals, cards move to free cells, and cards are played home automatically.
editions.issues: At 640x480 the window is wider than the screen, so the last column is cut off.

editions.works: F2 deals a new game, and clicking a card and then a home cell moves it there.
The clubhouse screen appears and the game moves on to the first tee.
editions.issues: Hitting shots has not been verified.

editions.works: New Game starts dropping pieces at the game's normal speed, and the arrow keys move the falling piece.

demo.label: Freeware (Funpack.Net collection, Classic DOS Games archive)

editions.works: You can pick a driver and a track, start a time-trial race and drive the car with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: The race takes a long time to load, and the game runs slowly enough that a quick key tap can get missed.

editions.works: You can make a player ID, start the single-player story, watch the intro cutscene and get into the first mission.
editions.issues: The ground and distant cliffs draw far too dark, and it has not been tried in the browser.

editions.works: Puzzles display with readable score, timer and target fields, and the puzzle buttons work.
The original installer runs to completion, and the game gets into the Wild Demo level with the player, the HUD and the opening tutorial message on screen, at about 30 fps in a browser benchmark.
editions.issues: Driving or walking around the level has not been tested, and the installer has to be run as separate steps because the emulator does not launch its child programs.

editions.works: The installer and launcher work, New Game on Easy gets into the first corridor with textures and the HUD, and you can walk and look around with the OpenGL, Direct3D and software renderers.
editions.issues: Switching the renderer from inside the game freezes it for good, and the software renderer is very slow in the browser.

editions.works: From the setup screen you can start a new game, load the first mission and fly down the canyon with the cockpit HUD and radar, banking with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: The setup screen keeps redrawing itself and burns CPU, its buttons show magenta corners, and sound and the Direct3D mode have not been checked.

editions.works: A new game starts from the main menu, and you can walk Corvus around the first area and turn him with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: Combat, later levels, sound and the browser version have not been tested.

titles.title: Heroes of Might and Magic II

editions.works: You can start a standard game, open the hero screen and walk your hero across the adventure map while the camera scrolls.
editions.issues: In the browser the hero walks about five times slower than it should, the map can flash a stretched picture for a moment while scrolling, and battles have not been tested.

titles.title: Heroes of Might and Magic III

editions.works: The demo reaches the adventure map, where clicking moves the hero, opens a treasure chest and collecting the gold updates the treasury.
The OpenGL version reaches the main menu, starts a new Paladin mission, and the player can turn and walk in first person.
editions.issues: The first level load spends a very long time building models before play starts; combat, sound and the software version were not checked.

editions.works: Through the menus and briefing into the restaurant mission, where Agent 47 walks, turns and runs with the numpad controls and the world keeps rendering for several minutes.
The demo installs, starts a single-player mission past the intro, and the Mothership can be selected on the battlefield with the mouse.
A new game starts from the title menu and the knight walks around the 3D street under keyboard control.
editions.issues: Gameplay is CPU-heavy and may run slowly; level completion and sound quality were not checked.

editions.works: From the original install, a character can be created, the first tavern area reached, the character walked around, and a quicksave written and reloaded.
editions.issues: The chapter narration text is blank, and play from the original install has not yet been confirmed in the browser.

editions.works: The original installer runs, the title menu starts a game, and Harold moves on the tower with the arrow keys.
The 3D menu leads through the mission briefing into the first gun-turret phase, where the turret turns and fires, including with touch controls in the browser.
In the browser the demo mission loads into the cockpit and the car drives and fires.
The original installer runs, a new game starts on Level 1, and the paddle follows the mouse and launches the ball, at about 60 frames per second.
The original installer completes, a new single-player game starts from the menu, and Jazz runs and shoots enemies in the first level; a two-player LAN join also connects.
Levels can be played with the mouse, a cleared level advances to the next one, and high scores and game over work.
editions.issues: Some dialogs look different from Windows (smaller fonts, and the level-complete popup is partly clipped).

editions.works: A picture opens and is cut into pieces, and pieces can be dragged around the board.
editions.issues: The piece is not drawn while it is being dragged; placing a piece in its correct slot has not been tested.

editions.works: A picture can be opened as a puzzle and pieces dragged with the mouse lock into place on the right cell.
editions.issues: The piece-lock sound does not play.

editions.works: The main menu and first level work; Anne turns, walks and sidesteps, and the level also loads in the browser.
editions.issues: Running straight into crates can tip the camera over, possibly the game's own physics.

editions.works: The demo starts a new game from the menu, plays its intro cut-scene and lets you walk and turn in the first level.
editions.issues: The first level takes a very long time to load, and combat and sound have not been checked.

editions.works: Puzzle selection works, the board appears, and blocks slide when dragged with the mouse.
The menu works from the keyboard and on the first level the paddle moves left and right and launches the ball.
editions.issues: Only the opening of the first level was tried; longer play and sound are unchecked.

editions.works: The menu works and a single-player match runs, with your army following the cursor you steer from the keyboard.
editions.issues: Network play reaches the waiting room but starting a networked match has not been shown.

editions.works: The original installer completes, and a VS fight can be set up from the menus and played with movement and attacks.
editions.issues: Only a reduced set of three fighters fits in memory, and switching to fullscreen with Alt+Enter crashes the game, so use the page's fullscreen button.

editions.works: The game opens its tutorial board, and you can select a marble with the mouse and move it with the arrow keys.
editions.issues: The game window is slightly larger than the screen, so its right and bottom edges are cut off; sound is unchecked.

editions.works: The demo's setup program starts and accepts the Install click.
editions.issues: Setup crashes during its system test, so the game itself has not been reached.

editions.works: The mode menu works with the mouse and the game reaches play, including on a phone touchscreen using trackpad-style dragging.
The GOG installer runs and its bundled ScummVM starts the game and shows its opening sequence; a manual run reached the first room under player control.
editions.issues: Player control was only seen in one manual run, and the game needs ScummVM's software renderer setting to show a picture.

demo.label: Freeware full game (ScummVM, with Revolution's permission)

editions.issues: The game stops during startup before opening a window because a bundled library needs system functions that are not available yet.

editions.works: The chamber starts with bouncing balls, clicking moves the gate, and balls pass through the opening.
The menu, a new game, the intro and the tutorial level render and respond to keyboard and mouse in the browser.
editions.issues: Skipping the long intro is unreliable from run to run, and jumping has not been seen working in play.

editions.works: You can create a pilot, go through Instant Action and deploy into a mission with the cockpit view running.
editions.issues: In the browser the mission runs at only about five frames per second.

editions.works: The player starts and opens its main window.
editions.issues: Playing media has not been checked.

editions.works: The main menu, new game and difficulty screens work and the first level plays with keyboard and on-screen touch controls in the browser.
editions.issues: The game reports it cannot read the audio CD, so music is missing, and speed has not been measured.

editions.works: An offline game against three computer players can be dealt, cards passed and tricks played.
All seven 3D screensavers draw their animated scenes, including lighting, textures and translucent shadows.
editions.issues: Organic Art spends most of its time loading the next scene, and the browser's hardware-accelerated mode has not been rechecked since September.

editions.works: All four screensavers show their photo slideshows with slides and crossfades, both from the command line and in the browser.
The savers start and show their background picture.
editions.issues: The animated 3D scene is never drawn, so the picture stays still.

editions.works: The menus work and a Quick Race in Chicago can be started and driven with the mouse to the first checkpoint.

demo.label: Trial (archive.org; Microsoft trial EULA permits non-commercial redistribution)

editions.works: The menus work and a race starts and can be driven from the keyboard in the software renderer.
editions.issues: The pre-race screen shows a blank name where it should say your controller is the keyboard.

demo.label: Trial (archive.org; Microsoft trial EULA permits non-commercial redistribution)

editions.works: Moorhuhn 1, 2 and Winter Edition reach a shooting round in the browser, and aimed shots score points.
Starts, takes a player name (including Backspace), walks through the menus and loads the Stunt Quarry race with rider, terrain and HUD drawn.
editions.issues: Riding the bike during a race has not been checked yet, and loading the race takes about a minute.

editions.works: Both the demo and the retail CD reach a 3D level where units can be selected and moved, with music and in-level sound, running at the game's 30 frames per second cap.
editions.issues: Key and mouse presses have to be held for a moment to register.

editions.works: The Special Edition 3dfx demo races and drives with road, terrain and cars drawn; the original NFS II demo reaches its menu and a race that responds to the throttle.

titles.title: Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit
